ModifyHandDraw.rationale: BoomingConch.cs:15-31 adds CardsVar(2).IntValue on the owner's turn 1 in an Elite room; the sim's _in_elite_first_turn (booming_conch.py:17-24) checks `combat.room_type == RoomType.ELITE and self.turn <= 1` and adds CARDS = 2. Same dispatcher and turn position as relic/bag_of_preparation and relic/big_mushroom (player.py:171 = turn_structure step 20). The C# room read is `player.RunState.CurrentRoom` and the sim's is the combat's own room_type -- the same room while a combat is in progress. Executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch2): an Elite turn-1 hand is 7 (base 5 + 2).

AfterSideTurnStart.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The energy amount and the Elite/turn-1 conditions are right (executed: Elite turn-1 energy is 4 = base 3 + 1), but the hook slot is wrong and the grant bypasses the energy-gain modifier chain.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C#'s AfterSideTurnStart is post-draw (turn_structure step 23); the sim uses on_player_turn_start, which the turn-order probe places PRE-draw, four steps earlier
guards.issue: The relic's own two halves end up on opposite sides of the draw from the source's arrangement: C# adds the cards (ModifyHandDraw, step 20), draws, and only then grants the energy (step 23); the sim grants the energy at step ~19 and then draws. Anything that reads the player's energy during the turn-1 draw sees 3 in C# and 4 in the sim. REACHABILITY (DORMANT): the readers would be an on-draw card effect or a modify_hand_draw listener that branches on current energy, and no ported content does either -- the ported modify_hand_draw listeners (bag_of_preparation, big_mushroom, this relic) all branch on turn number and room type only. Porting an energy-reading draw effect makes it live. Same family as relic/bag_of_marbles' G1, which is why the correct sim slot for AfterSideTurnStart is on_player_turn_startED.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# grants the energy through PlayerCmd.GainEnergy, which runs Hook.ModifyEnergyGain and Hook.AfterModifyingEnergyGain; the sim assigns player.energy directly (booming_conch.py:34)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PlayerCmd.GainEnergy (PlayerCmd.cs) computes `finalAmount = Hook.ModifyEnergyGain(...)`, awaits Hook.AfterModifyingEnergyGain over the modifiers, and grants only `if (finalAmount > 0)`. The sim HAS that chain -- EnergyCmd.gain (cmds.py) calls hooks.modify_energy_gain(player, amount) before adding, and relic/art_of_war uses it -- but booming_conch.py:34 does `player.energy += self.ENERGY` and skips it. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the reason is a timing accident worth recording): the sim's one ported modify_energy_gain listener is NoEnergyGainPower (powers.py:554-558), which returns 0 for its owner, and it is applied to the PLAYER by the ported card expect_a_fight. Under it, C# would grant 0 and the sim grants 1. But NoEnergyGainPower expires at the owner's turn end (powers.py:559-561) and Booming Conch fires only on turn <= 1 -- before any card can be played -- so the two can never overlap today. Porting any monster or relic that applies NoEnergyGain before the player's first turn, or any modify_energy_gain listener without the turn-end expiry, makes it live.

guards.rationale: The `player != base.Owner` / `shuffler == base.Owner` / `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player. The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState), so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N2: Flash() and the Energy hover tip (BoomingConch.cs:7, 40)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
